name: AZD9550

lead: AZD9550 is an experimental injectable drug that activates both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, developed by AstraZeneca for obesity.
It has been through phase 1 and phase 2 trials, including a combination with AZD6234, but no results have been published.

paras: GLP-1 activation reduces appetite, while glucagon receptor activation is intended to add effects on energy use and the liver. This is as described by the compound class; no AZD9550-specific data are public.
No published safety data were found. It is not approved and is only available in clinical trials.

lead: AZD9550 is an investigational GLP-1/glucagon receptor dual agonist from AstraZeneca, given by subcutaneous injection and studied for obesity and related liver disease. [1][2]

Evidence is limited to early-phase trial registrations. Phase 1 and phase 2 studies have tested it alone and in combination with AZD6234, an amylin agonist; no results from these trials have been published in the sources reviewed. [2][3]

paras: A single-ascending-dose phase 1 trial in healthy participants (48 participants, started May 2023) was registered under a non-alcoholic steatohepatitis condition. [1] A phase 1/2 trial examined safety of AZD9550 alone and with AZD6234 in people with overweight or obesity with or without type 2 diabetes (166 participants). [2]

A phase 2 weight-loss trial (377 participants) compared the combination of AZD9550 and AZD6234 with placebo and with each drug alone, and is registered as completed. [3] Other studies cover hepatic impairment, formulation bioavailability, oral contraceptive interaction and a platform study in Chinese participants. [4][5][6][7] No results have been published.

timeline.event: Phase 2 combination weight-loss trial with AZD6234 starts. [3]
